candidates.content_text:
Company Description
Work with Us. Change the World.
At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.
There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
Play a key role in delivering a diverse range of exciting infrastructure projects across roads, commercial and industrial developments, sports, resources, water infrastructure, defence and renewable energy.
You’ll be responsible for developing high-quality civil design models, drawings and technical documentation across projects ranging from local roads and parklands to mine sites, dams, substations, BESS facilities, solar farms and wind farms.
What you'll be doing
- Develop detailed civil design models using 12d Model, including earthworks, roadworks, surface grading, DDA pedestrian access, pavements, drainage networks, culverts and open channels.
- Deliver designs across water and sewer infrastructure, including pipelines, water and sewer reticulation and pump stations, as well as stormwater and bio-retention systems.
- Produce high-quality drawings and documentation using AutoCAD, aligned with client requirements, industry standards and relevant government and regulatory requirements.
- Undertake geometry assessments and swept-path analysis to ensure designs are practical, safe and fit for purpose.
- Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary project teams, coordinating civil interfaces with architectural, structural, landscape, hydraulic, geotechnical, mechanical, electrical, communications, process and environmental disciplines.
- Contribute to design and model reviews, clash detection and safety-in-design activities, ensuring quality is embedded throughout the design process.
- Prepare and review technical inputs for Bills of Quantities, balancing safety, constructability, operational requirements and cost efficiency.
- Work directly with regional project teams to understand requirements, resolve technical queries and deliver work packages to agreed scope, programme and budget.
- Support quality assurance by checking your own work and, where appropriate, reviewing the work of less experienced team members in line with AECOM's quality procedures.
- Contribute to the ongoing improvement of our civil design capability through standard details, design libraries, digital workflows, lessons learned and continuous improvement initiatives.
Qualifications
What you'll bring
We’re looking for someone with a background in civil design and drafting who is keen to contribute to diverse, multidisciplinary projects. You don’t need to tick every box, if you have the right experience and attitude, we’d love to hear from you.
- Civil Engineering qualification (Associate Degree, Diploma, Advanced Diploma or Degree).
- 2+ years’ civil design and drafting experience, ideally across urban, rural, commercial, residential, industrial or mining projects.
- Strong experience in road geometry, pavements, earthworks, grading and drainage design.
- Advanced AutoCAD skills, with experience in 12d Model and vehicle tracking.
- Experience developing civil drawings, models and quantity take-offs.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, including working with multidisciplinary and international teams.
- Experience with water and sewer infrastructure, including reticulation, pump stations, rising mains, pipelines and reservoirs, is highly regarded.
- Familiarity with relevant Australian standards and guidelines, including Austroads, QUDM, WSAA and IPWEA, is desirable.
- Experience taking designs from concept through to construction documentation, as well as working within multidisciplinary model review environments.
- Experience mentoring junior or cadet drafters and contributing to design capability development is advantageous.
You must be an Australian citizen and be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Baseline security clearance.

Reporting to the Deputy Director Engineering, the Civil Design Drafter role is responsible for completing civil designs, drafting work and documentation for road infrastructure projects across the Big Build Roads (BBR) program from concept design to construction. The role requires thorough understanding of DTP's Infrastructure Drafting Standards and project handover requirements ensuring design models, plans and documentation are compliant. Join us in building better connections for Victoria by:

You'll assist with the inspection, maintenance and renewal of Council's civil infrastructure assets, investigate defects and service requests, coordinate maintenance activities and contribute to the delivery of infrastructure upgrade projects. You'll also support contract administration, manage asset data, prepare technical reports and provide engineering advice to both internal and external stakeholders.
This is a varied role that combines technical engineering, asset management, project coordination and stakeholder engagement.
About you
We're looking for a motivated and customer-focused engineer who enjoys problem-solving and working collaboratively to deliver practical outcomes.
To be successful, you will have:
 - A Bachelor of Civil Engineering (or equivalent recognised by Engineers Australia).
 - A current NSW Driver's Licence.

 - Knowledge of asset management principles, condition assessments and infrastructure maintenance practices.
 - Strong communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with contractors, residents, government agencies and internal stakeholders.
 - Experience preparing technical reports, specifications, estimates and project documentation.
 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office and exposure to asset management systems, GIS, AutoCAD or similar engineering software.
 - Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
Highly regarded
Experience in Local Government, civil infrastructure construction and management, street lighting management, GIS, AutoCAD and infrastructure renewal programs will be highly regarded.
Why join us?
This is an excellent opportunity to build your engineering career while contributing to meaningful projects that improve community infrastructure and public spaces. You'll gain exposure to a broad range of asset management, maintenance and renewal activities while working within a supportive and collaborative team environment.
If you're passionate about civil infrastructure and want to help shape the future of one of Sydney's most vibrant communities, we'd love to hear from you.

Join an established civil contractor delivering a $3.7m Brisbane road project. Monday-Friday role hands on.
Your new company
An established civil contractor delivering projects across road construction, land development and infrastructure is seeking an experienced Project Engineer to join their Brisbane-based team.
With a strong track record across road upgrades, bulk earthworks, pavements, underground services and civil infrastructure, this contractor has built a reputation for delivering quality projects while maintaining a practical and collaborative working environment.
This is an excellent opportunity for a Project Engineer looking to step away from the consistently extended hours often associated with larger Tier 1 environments and join a contractor offering family-friendly Monday-to-Friday hours, hands-on project involvement and genuine responsibility for project delivery.
Your new role
You will join the project team delivering a road infrastructure project, working closely with the Project Manager, supervisors, subcontractors and suppliers.
The project offers a varied civil scope including:
- Bulk earthworks
- Road and pavement construction
- Water main works
- Stormwater infrastructure
- Electrical realignments
- Unbound pavements
- Asphalt works
- Concrete works
- Road furniture
You'll be involved from early works and mobilisation through to construction, completion and handover, giving you exposure across the full project lifecycle.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating day-to-day engineering and construction activities
- Managing bulk earthworks, road and pavement works
- Coordinating subcontractors, suppliers, plant and materials
- Reviewing drawings, specifications and technical documentation
- Supporting project planning, programming and construction sequencing
- Preparing and managing ITPs and QA documentation
- Coordinating inspections, testing and quality requirements
- Assisting with procurement and subcontractor packages
- Managing technical queries and resolving construction issues
- Assisting with quantities, variations, progress claims and cost control
- Ensuring safety, environmental, quality and project requirements are maintained
- Supporting project completion, documentation and handover
What you'll need to succeed
- Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering
- Proven experience as a Project Engineer within civil construction
- Previous TMR project experience
- Strong experience delivering road construction projects
- Experience across bulk earthworks and pavement construction
- Strong understanding of ITPs, QA and civil project documentation
- Experience coordinating subcontractors and site activities
- Ability to interpret civil drawings, specifications and technical documentation
- Strong organisation, communication and problem-solving skills
- Full Australian working rights
What you'll get in return
- Monday-to-Friday working arrangements
- Brisbane southside project location
- Varied road and civil infrastructure scope
- Hands-on involvement across the full project lifecycle
- Close working relationship with experienced Project Managers and site leadership
- Long-term opportunities across a diverse civil project pipeline
- Supportive team environment with a strong focus on safety and quality
 What to do now

candidates.content_text:
At Goldsmith we are passionate about our industry and committed to delivering high-quality solutions that add real value for our customers. We’re more than just a business we pride ourselves on our talented team members who work together to achieve outstanding results. 
We are currently seeking a Estimator to join our team and play a key role in securing and delivering projects across Victoria and beyond. As a part of this role, you will lead the preparation and submission of accurate, competitive tenders for civil and bulk earthwork projects. This is your opportunity to take your career to the next level and contribute to large-scale, industry-leading projects. If you have a strong technical background in civil construction and bulk earthworks and an eye for detail, we’d love to hear from you!
About the Role
As a Estimator, your initial responsibilities will include:
- Leading the preparation, review, and submission of tenders that maximise success and profitability.
- Identifying and assessing new tender opportunities, making informed bid/no-bid recommendations.
- Performing accurate quantity take-offs, cost estimating, and risk analysis.
- Liaising and negotiating with suppliers, subcontractors, and consultants to secure the best value and minimise risk.
- Developing construction programs and producing high-quality tender documentation.
- Collaborating closely with project managers, engineers, and clients to ensure clear communication and project success.
About you
To be considered for this role the successful applicant must have:
- 3-5 years of proven estimating experience in civil construction, bulk earthworks, or related industries.
- Expertise in industry-standard estimating software and Microsoft Project.
- Strong commercial acumen and attention to detail.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to build strong relationships.
- Ability to manage multiple tenders simultaneously with strong organisational skills.
- Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or related field preferred (or significant equivalent experience).
- Valid driver’s licence.
- Valid working rights in Australia
What next?
To apply - just submit your CV.
As part of the application, you'll be asked about your experience to date to help us better understand your suitability for the position.
At Goldsmith we prioritize workplace health and safety, and therefore, applicants must be willing to undergo pre-employment medical assessments, including drug and alcohol testing.
Goldsmith is an equal opportunity employer with a strong commitment to diversity. We encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and female candidates to apply.
If you're ready to join a dynamic team focused on achieving project success together, apply now!
If you believe you possess additional skills that could be valuable to our team but may not align with the listed roles, please don't hesitate to reach out to the hr@goldsmith.com.au
For more information about the company visit: www.goldsmith.com.au

Strengthen and Extend the Life of Australia's Infrastructure
Freyssinet is a global leader in specialised civil engineering, delivering innovative solutions in structural remediation, concrete repair, asset protection, strengthening, cathodic protection, waterproofing and post-tensioning.
Due to continued growth across our Remedial division, we are seeking a motivated Site Engineer to join our Victorian team.
This is an exciting opportunity to work on challenging infrastructure projects across Victoria, gaining exposure to a wide variety of remediation and structural repair works.
The Role
Reporting to the Construction Manager, you will play a key role in the successful delivery of remedial projects by supporting planning, execution and site operations.
Key responsibilities include:
- Assisting with the management and delivery of remediation projects
- Coordinating subcontractors, suppliers and site personnel
- Monitoring project progress, costs and quality outcomes
- Preparing work packs, methodologies, ITPs and project documentation
- Ensuring works are completed safely and in line with project specifications
- Conducting site inspections and maintaining quality records
- Assisting with procurement, scheduling and forecasting activities
- Building strong relationships with clients and project stakeholders
About You
- Degree qualified in Civil Engineering, Construction Management or a related discipline
- 3 years' + experience in civil, structural, remedial or construction projects
- Strong organisational and communication skills
- Ability to work independently and as part of a project team
- Willingness to travel to Tasmania and South Australia if required
- Full Australian Driver's Licence
- Strong commitment to safety and quality
What We Offer
- Exposure to some of Australia's most complex infrastructure and remediation projects
- Opportunity to develop specialist expertise in structural repairs and asset preservation
- Career progression within a global engineering organisation
- Supportive and experienced project teams
- Competitive salary package
- Travel opportunities across multiple states
- Ongoing training and professional development
Why Join Freyssinet?
- Be part of a team dedicated to sustaining and enhancing Australia’s vital infrastructure.
- Work on high-value, complex remedial projects with a globally recognized leader.
- Enjoy career development opportunities and exposure to iconic infrastructure projects.
- Supportive work culture, and a strong focus on safety and innovation.
Ready to Join Us?
If you're ready to take on an exciting new challenge and become part of an innovative and supportive team, we'd love to hear from you!
Apply today and be a part of shaping Australia’s future with Freyssinet!
How to Apply: If you are a motivated professional ready to take on a dynamic role with the opportunity to travel and work on impactful projects across Australia, we encourage you to apply. 
Please send your updated resume/CV to Rachel Greenway at rgreenway@freyssinet.com.au
Join Us in Building a Better Future! At Freyssinet, we are committed to diversity and inclusion, believing that diverse perspectives enhance our engineering solutions. We seek top talent based on skills, motivation, and cultural fit. We encourage applications from all demographic groups, with recruitment decisions made purely on merit.
